meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: She's a lecturer.
I haven't heard of her.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'yesterday', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Yesterday I was at home.
Yesterday was Friday.

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: What did you say?
Excuse me, where's the metro?
Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
I'm doing my homework.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'олнце'). Common neuter noun meaning 'sun' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мы идём вверх, прямо к солнцу.
examples.trans: We are walking up, straight to the sun.
Thank you, sweetheart. Go on, Yulya, work.

meanings.note: Borrowed from Latin agent/instrument noun in '-tor' ('трансформатор'). Common masculine noun meaning 'transformer' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Sun. Transformer.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новый трансформатор.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new transformer.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Grab him!
It needs a wash.
Four-eyes! Grab him!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'oh, ah', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh, you greedy thing!
Oh, how beautiful!

examples.text: Ах ты, жадина! А у тебя есть телефон?
examples.trans: Oh, you greedy thing! And have you got a phone?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'something; somehow', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Has something happened?
Somehow I'm tired.
I can't see it somehow.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: He says nasty things about me.
She knows everything about everyone.

examples.text: Как интересно! А в Москве ты про меня гадости рассказываешь.
examples.trans: How interesting! And in Moscow you go around saying nasty things about me.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'love' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is all for love!

examples.text: Я умоляю вас, доктор! Это всё ради любви!
examples.trans: I beg you, Doctor! This is all for love!
Love is like war.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'верное').

examples.trans: Well, probably somewhere in the archive.
He has probably already come home.

examples.text: Наверное, что-то серьёзное у вас. Девочка уже две недели лежит в областной клинике!
examples.trans: It must be something serious for you. The girl has been lying in the regional clinic for two weeks already!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: I didn't understand.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?
I understand you.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common feminine noun meaning 'girl, little girl' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Girl, pass me the sugar, please.
A little girl is playing in the yard.

examples.text: Очень плохой кофе. Девочка, дай сахар, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Very bad coffee. Girl, pass me the sugar, please.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto; for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'state support' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я не понял, девочки, вы что, на гособеспечении?
examples.trans: I do not get it, girls, are you on state welfare or what?

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новое гособеспечение.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new state support.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: He drives fast.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

examples.text: Разговорчики, лейтенант Соколов! Быстро на рабочее место.
examples.trans: That's enough talk, Lieutenant Sokolov! Back to your desk, quickly.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to work', paired with 'поработать'.

examples.trans: I work as mayor.
Where do you work?

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'рубок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'stump, stub' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Get to work fast, you stumps!

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новый обрубок.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new stump.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share with everyone.
I'm with Dad.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.
Dad is already home.
I'm already home.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'долбаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get fed up, exhausted (slang)'.

related.gloss: to to get fed up (prefixed perfective)
not to to get fed up (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Я уже задолбался угадывать, что с ним.
examples.trans: I am sick and tired of guessing what is wrong with him.

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет задолбаться без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to get fed up without a reason.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'гадывать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to guess'.

examples.text: Я уже задолбался угадывать, что с ним.
examples.trans: I am sick and tired of guessing what is wrong with him.

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет угадывать без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to guess without a reason.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to give; (imperative) let's', paired with 'дать'.

examples.trans: Let's talk.
He gives me a book.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

принять.gloss: to receive, to see (a visitor); to accept

meanings.en: to receive, to see (a visitor); to accept
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to receive, to see (a visitor); to accept', paired with 'принимать'.

examples.trans: Thanks for seeing me.
She'll see you tomorrow.
You recognised me. Thanks for seeing me.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I'm just tired.
It's easy.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'madman' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is an absolute madman.
Quickly! Pack everything up fast!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'head' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I have a headache.
Mum will tear my head off.

examples.text: Какая тебе опергруппа? Мне твоя мать голову оторвёт.
examples.trans: What field team? Your mother will tear my head off.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'oneself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I feel good.
He only thinks about himself.

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'стучать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to knock'.

examples.trans: Go knock on your own head.

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет постучать без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to knock without a reason.
